paper_metadata.title: LatentQGAN: A Hybrid QGAN with Classical Convolutional Autoencoder

summary: The paper introduces LatentQGAN, a hybrid quantum‑classical GAN where a classical convolutional autoencoder compresses MNIST images to a 5×8 latent space and a quantum generator composed of five 4‑qubit PQCs (7 variational layers, 140 parameters) generates latent vectors. Experiments with 2048 shots on IBM’s ibm_quebec processor report Frechet Distance scores of 33, 39, and 29 on a simulator and 38, 43, and 34 on hardware for MNIST classes 0, 5, and 9 respectively, outperforming prior QGAN variants in their comparisons.

experiments.description: Hybrid LatentQGAN for MNIST image generation: a classical convolutional autoencoder compresses images into a latent space, and a hybrid quantum-classical GAN trains a quantum generator on the latent representation; evaluated on simulator and IBM Eagle quantum hardware for classes 0, 5, and 9.

algorithm.variant: LatentQGAN (hybrid QGAN with classical convolutional autoencoder)
algorithm.ansatz: parameterized quantum circuits with rotation gates and CZ entangling layers; partial measurement with ancillary qubits
algorithm.convergence_criteria: optimal number of iterations determined empirically; training evaluated up to 1000 iterations, with best FD typically between 350 and 700 iterations
algorithm.parameter_initialization: identical noise vectors and initial parameters used for simulator and quantum computer comparison; otherwise not specified

problem_formulation.encoding_details: MNIST images are compressed by a convolutional autoencoder into a normalized latent space of size 5 x 8; each row is generated by one quantum sub-generator and then normalized to satisfy generator constraints
problem_formulation.objective_function: GAN minimax objective with binary cross-entropy loss for generator/discriminator; autoencoder trained with mean squared error reconstruction loss
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: latent-space normalization per line; post-selection on ancillary qubits equal to |0> to emulate partial measurement

problem_instance.description: Handwritten digit image generation in latent space

dataset_specification.description: 28 x 28 grayscale handwritten digits; experiments reported for classes 0, 5, and 9

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: images compressed by convolutional autoencoder into latent representation; latent vectors normalized line by line
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Frechet Distance (FD) used to compare generated samples with ground truth; visual inspection of generated images; comparison against QPatchGAN, MosaiQ, LatentGAN, and RandomDecoder; quantum computer results reported for a single run using identical noise vectors and initial parameters as simulator trainings

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: autoencoder training on MNIST before QGAN training
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: decoder reconstructs images from generated latent vectors

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: FD improves up to mid-training then degrades after about 700 iterations

results.value: MNIST 28 x 28 grayscale images; reported classes 0, 5, 9

speedup_claims.conditions: to achieve comparable results / minimal FD
speedup_claims.caveats: Claim is based on iteration count, not wall-clock time; comparison is against a simulator-based MosaiQ result and the paper does not provide a full matched protocol for all baselines.
The paper reports empirical improvements and reduced quantum resources, but no asymptotic complexity or proven quantum speedup.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: not applicable; no asymptotic advantage analyzed
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not specified; paper provides no complexity analysis or scaling argument for quantum advantage.
limiting_factors: No complexity or scaling analysis versus classical generative models
Very small circuits (4 qubits per generator circuit)
Hybrid pipeline dominated by classical autoencoder and discriminator
Evaluation on small benchmark (MNIST latent space)
Single‑run hardware results with limited statistical validation

notes: num_qubits inferred from 5 sub-generators × 4 qubits each = 20 total qubits; paper explicitly states five 4-qubit quantum circuits.
hardware.type reported as real quantum computer on IBM Eagle processor; mapped to real_qpu_superconducting.
circuit_depth reported as 7 layers in the variational circuits.
speedup_order set to none_proven because the paper reports empirical improvements but no asymptotic complexity analysis.
Authors claim improved image quality versus prior QGAN approaches and classical LatentGAN with equal parameter counts, but they do not claim computational quantum advantage.
Comparisons focus on Frechet Distance and visual quality rather than runtime or scaling.
Problem size (latent MNIST generation) is small and dominated by classical components.
